## Update your operating system first

At home, update your computer to the latest version of its operating system.

Restart the computer after the update.

::: {.warning}
An outdated system can produce mysterious errors that your classmates do not encounter.
:::

## Install R before installing Positron

1. Go to [cloud.r-project.org](https://cloud.r-project.org/).
2. Choose your operating system.
3. Download and install the current release of R.

If R is already installed, update it before the course begins.

::: {.key-point}
Positron requires R 4.2 or newer.
:::

::: {.notes}
- Positron installation prerequisites: https://positron.posit.co/install
- The Comprehensive R Archive Network: https://cloud.r-project.org/
:::

## Install Positron

1. Go to [positron.posit.co/install](https://positron.posit.co/install).
2. Choose the installer for your operating system.
3. Accept the licence agreement and follow the standard installation steps.

On macOS, choose the download that matches your computer: **Apple Silicon** or **Intel**.

::: {.key-point}
Positron includes Quarto, which we use for all coursework. You do not need to install it separately.
:::

::: {.notes}
- Install Positron: https://positron.posit.co/install
:::

## Confirm that Positron can run R

Open Positron. In the **Interpreter picker** at the top right, select an R session.

Then run this in the Console:

```{r}
#| label: r-version
R.version.string
```

You should see an R version of **4.2 or newer** and no error message.

::: {.notes}
- Managing interpreters in Positron: https://positron.posit.co/managing-interpreters.html
:::

## Download and extract the course folder

Download **c407.zip** from **Canvas**.

Extract it to a folder that is easy to find.

::: {.warning}
On Windows, right-click the ZIP file and choose **Extract All…**. Opening the ZIP file is not the same as extracting it.
:::

## What is in the course folder

| Folder or file | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `data/` | Course datasets. Read from here; never edit these files. |
| `scripts/` | Your Quarto documents (`.qmd`). |
| `temp/` | Disposable output, such as saved figures. |
| `_quarto.yml` | Makes code run from the `c407` folder. Do not move it. |
| `AGENTS.md` | Course rules for AI coding tools. |
| `CLAUDE.md` | Makes Claude Code read `AGENTS.md`. |
| `README.md` | A summary of this setup. |

## Check that the data were extracted

In the extracted **c407** folder, open the **data** folder.

### How many `.rds` files are there?

::: {.answer-grid}
**A.** 1

**B.** 2

**C.** 3

**D.** 4

**E.** 5
:::

::: {.notes}
Answer: **E. 5.** `2016_census_pumf_ind.rds`, `2021_census_pumf_ind.rds`, `bca262.rds`, `pindex_w.rds`, and `renter_l.rds`.
:::

## Open the c407 folder as a workspace

In Positron, choose **File → Open Folder…** and select the extracted **c407** folder.

Opening the folder:

- makes **c407** the workspace;
- shows its files in the Explorer; and
- sets the R working directory to that folder.

::: {.key-point}
Always open the **c407 folder** itself, not a folder inside it.
:::

::: {.notes}
- Positron workspaces: https://positron.posit.co/migrate-rstudio-rproj.html
:::

## Install the course packages once

Run this once in the **Console**:

```{r}
#| label: install
#| eval: false
install.packages(c(
  "tidyverse", "rmarkdown", "sf", "tmap", "maptiles", "cancensus",
  "cansim", "VancouvR", "tidygeocoder", "fixest", "modelsummary"
))
```

Installation can take several minutes. Rerun it if you get a new computer or a new version of R.

::: {.key-point}
Install packages in the Console, never inside a Quarto document.
:::

## Use this start-up routine every class

1. Open **Positron**.
2. Open the **c407 folder** as your workspace.
3. Confirm that an **R interpreter** is active.
4. Open the class `.qmd` file in `scripts/`.

::: {.key-point}
Keep your documents, data, and outputs together inside the course folder.
:::

## Preview: an AI coding agent at work

Later in the course, you will work with an AI coding agent in Positron, such as **Codex** or **Claude Code**.

- It reads the files in your `c407` folder, including `AGENTS.md`.
- It writes code, runs it, and fixes its own errors.

Today, you only watch. Do not install anything yet.

::: {.notes}
- Demo on my machine. Students install an agent in "Working with AI".
- Run it in a fresh copy of the `c407` folder. No API key is needed: the demo uses `data/2021_census_pumf_ind.rds` and `data/provinces.geojson`.
- Claude Code reads `CLAUDE.md`, which imports `AGENTS.md`. With Claude Code, run `/memory` to confirm that the course rules loaded.
- Rehearse with these exact prompts on the demo machine, including rendering. Keep the rehearsal output as a fallback.
:::

## Ask for a map

```text
Create scripts/ai_demo.qmd. Using the 2021 Census PUMF and the province
boundaries in data/, map the share of young adults who live with their
parents, by province.
```

::: {.notes}
- "Young adults" is deliberately vague. `AGENTS.md` tells the agent to ask before making choices that affect the analysis. If it asks, put the question to the class first.
- Choices to look for in the agent's code:
  - Ages: Statistics Canada uses 20 to 34. The rehearsal used 25 to 34, which leaves out most students living at home. Ontario is 26% at 25 to 34 but 39% at 20 to 34.
  - "Living with parents": `CFSTAT` "Child of a couple" or "Child of a parent in a one-parent family". A young adult living with a parent and their own partner or child is a spouse or parent, not a child.
  - Weights: shares should use `WEIGHT`.
  - Map classes: tmap's default classes for 25 to 34 are 2 points wide, and their labels round down: Saskatchewan (13.3%) sits in a class labelled "12 - 13".
- Published figure for comparison: Statistics Canada reports that 35.1% of 20- to 34-year-olds lived with at least one parent in 2021, and 46.6% in Toronto. For the same ages, the PUMF gives 32.7% and 44%, because of the "child" definition. A different age range makes the comparison meaningless.
- Explanation trap: the agent may blame housing costs. Toronto also has many immigrant families living in multigenerational households, and Quebec's cities are lowest even though Montréal is large. At 25 to 34, Toronto is 31% and Québec City 8.5%.
- Source: [The Daily, 13 July 2022](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/daily-quotidien/220713/dq220713a-eng.htm).
:::

## Ask about change

```text
Where did the share increase most between the 2016 and 2021 censuses?
The 2016 PUMF is in data/.
```

::: {.notes}
- Traps to look for in the agent's code:
  - `CFSTAT` labels changed: 2016 says "Child of a lone parent", 2021 "Child of a parent in a one-parent family". Reusing the 2021 labels gives 12.7% for 2016 instead of 18.2%, so the national rise looks like 7.3 points instead of 1.8. No error or warning.
  - Variable names changed too: 2016 has `TENUR` and `VALUE`; 2021 has `Tenur` and `Value`.
  - CMA names differ in dashes and spaces, and "Kelowna – Abbotsford" became "Kelowna – Abbotsford-Mission". A join by CMA name silently drops rows.
  - Sampling error: the PUMF is a 2.7% sample. P.E.I. and Northern Canada have standard errors of about 2.5 points.
- Rehearsal results (ages 25 to 34): Alberta +3.6 points, Manitoba +3.0, Saskatchewan +2.6, Ontario +1.6; B.C. +0.7. By CMA, Calgary +4.6.
- Explanation trap: average renter shelter costs rose 23% in B.C. and 21% in Ontario but 0% in Alberta and 1% in Saskatchewan. Rising rents run opposite to the change. Other candidates: the Prairie economies after the 2015 oil price drop, and the pandemic in May 2021.
:::

## Ask for slides

```text
Make a four-slide revealjs presentation of these findings.
Save it in scripts/ and render it.
```

## Who checks these results?

- Which ages count as "young adults"? Who counts as "living with parents"?
- Did the agent define it the same way in 2016 and 2021?
- Does the national share match Statistics Canada's published figure? If not, why not?
- Is housing cost the explanation? Compare where rents rose with where the share rose.

::: {.key-point}
You are responsible for every number you report, whoever wrote the code.
:::

## Learn to read code first

- For the first three weeks, write all your code without AI.
- Reading code is how you check what an AI gives you.
- In week 4, you will install an agent and practise checking its work.

::: {.key-point}
AI makes you faster only if you can tell when it is wrong.
:::
